body_markdown:
In recent years, automatic core cutters and high speed winders have significantly advanced productivity, with many line speeds reaching up to 8,500 feet per minute! This has revolutionized the paper winding business. Once a manual process with frequent machine bottlenecks, automation has turned paper mills into high speed, precision powerhouses. The only problem was the containerboard cores. They just couldn’t keep up.


Operators kept complaining about untimely snags, tears and stops on the machines. But, why?


Sonoco engineers set out to investigate and found three core reasons: automation, dimensional stability and critical speed. The speed part might have been obvious. Fiber cores simply were not designed to run so fast, so we needed to redesign one that could withstand the high torque and pressure. But what of the first two?


For automation, our engineers found a core needed to be more straightforward, as in **straight.** Literally. Straighter cores move more reliably through automatic core cutters, carts, saws and conveyor systems. Even slight warpage can jam up machines while cores travel around sharp 60 or 90 degree turns.


Secondly, cores needed better moisture resistance. Fiber-based cores are hygroscopic, meaning they gain and lose moisture easily. When they take on moisture, they expand; when they lose it, they contract. When hot paper winds around a core containing more moisture than the paper, the core can shrink inside the roll and create problems.


### Next-Generation Fiber Core Designed for Advanced Mill Operations


After years of research and testing[detailed in this white paper](https://www.sonoco.com/sites/default/files/images/site_images/SONARIS%20White%20Paper_Advanced%20Fiber%20Core.pdf) , engineers produced a highly advanced core manufacturing process that changed how cores are made from the inside-out.


The updated process led to Sonoco’s new **SONARIS™ advanced fiber core** . It’s much straighter than traditional, fiber-based products, even with longer lengths, and the propriety materials used to create SONARIS resist moisture more effectively, especially on fast machines often running much hotter than their predecessors. Test results showed up to a ***40 percent improvement in core warpage*** and ***100% more resistance to core chewouts*** .


About a handful of paper mill customers have already adopted SONARIS with remarkable success, realizing significant savings due to reduced product loss and/or machine downtime. More mills are following suit as they seek to maximize performance in today’s high speed winding environment.
